The two modes of reasoning I am to contrast are those that begin with first principles, and fundamental purposes, and those that start with immediate observations, and work backward.

In both cases there is the beginning, and the end. In the mode that starts from first principles and purposes, the mind, like the ship of Theseus, starts from the original wood and its planks, and proceeds with it, as the old Greek fable tells us, through all the vicissitudes of war and peace and change. But in the other mode, which I may call the mode of observation, the mind, like the ship of Diomedes, begins at the bottom, and takes off the bottom of the ship, and the planks above, and puts them together again in such a way that you cannot tell where the bottom was.

samples.prompt: Write three short anecdotal examples illustrating how unconventional or eccentric behavior can be more persuasive than eloquent rhetoric.
samples.generated:
Once a man of great eloquence and fine manners was sent to London for a commission from an influential lord. The man had a friend who was a painter, and he said to his friend: "I will take you with me; I will give you my commission, and you shall paint me in my shirt-clothes." The painter said that this would be most agreeable to him, and accordingly went with the man to London. The lord was highly pleased with the man in his shirt-clothes, and gave him more orders than ever before.

Another time a person was asked by a rich man to preach the gospel at his house. He said, "Let me stay here three months; I will write my sermons and read them to you daily." The rich man agreed and let him have a room. After three months, it was found that the rich man was very much better.

There is a story of a man who wished to have a certain place taken away from another. He said, "If you do not take my place, I will not take yours." The other man replied, "I cannot do without it." The first man said, "Then I will go without it," and departed.
